_meta.source: playbook-qa/fixtures/verdantis-nda-playbook.md (the dev copy). Every sentence in standardPosition, fallbacks, walkAwayPosition and acceptable[].sentences is verbatim from it after removing **, <u>, leading "> "/"• " and decoding &.
_meta.selfServe: All fallbacks selfServe false: Section 1A "There is no self-serve band and no set of self-serve fallbacks."
_meta.walkAwayWithApproval: Where a Walk-Away block only says a deviation is High/Medium/Low Risk needing named approval, the product prompt ("A concession the playbook accepts only with someone's approval is a fallback too") also allows it as a last approval fallback. Each such case is listed in that entry's `acceptable`; where the Fallback block says "Not applicable"/"None"/"Same as the Preferred Position", zero fallbacks is strict.

judgeRules.scope: Compare the extracted positions with this key. Text comparison ignores whitespace and markdown (**, *, <u>, leading "> " or "• ", & vs &). Label-only segments (a few heading words ending in ".", e.g. "Duration.", "Public Domain.", or a list number like "1.") may be added or omitted anywhere. Any other variation passes only if the entry's `acceptable` lists it.
judgeRules.matching: An extracted position covers a key position when it is about the same contract term, whatever its termName. If the key entry's `acceptable` allows a split or merge, judge the union of the covering positions: standard sentences joined, fallbacks in playbook order.
judgeRules.J1_missingPosition: FAIL if any key position has no extracted position covering its term.
judgeRules.J2_inaccurateStandard: FAIL if an extracted standardPosition (a) changes the meaning of the key standardPosition, (b) leaves out a key standard sentence that `acceptable` does not mark as omittable, or (c) adds a sentence that is not in the key standardPosition and not listed in `acceptable` as an allowed addition or move into the standard.
judgeRules.J3_fallbackTextNotExact: FAIL if an extracted fallback's text is not exactly the key fallback's sentences, allowing only the J-scope text normalisation and the `acceptable` variations (added, omitted, moved, split or merged sentences). FAIL if fallbacks are in a different order than the key, unless `acceptable` allows that order.
judgeRules.J4_fallbackCount: FAIL if the number of extracted fallbacks differs from the key's count, or falls outside the count `acceptable` allows (a "fallback count" line, or a variation that adds, splits or merges a rung). A missing key fallback or a fallback the key does not have is a FAIL. Where the key says "exactly zero", any fallback fails.
judgeRules.reportOnly: Never findings: isRequired differences; walk-away wording differences; extra positions that split or merge terms where `acceptable` allows; extra positions built only from sentences this file treats as non-positions (e.g. Section 7.2). Every fallback is expected to have selfServe false (Section 1A: "There is no self-serve band and no set of self-serve fallbacks."); a wrong selfServe flag and an entirely missing walk-away are findings, graded by the routine prompt.
judgeRules.verdict: Categories (Missing, Inaccurate, Hallucination) and severities (P0 fail, P1 warn) are defined in the Playbook QA routine prompt. This file defines what is expected and which variations are acceptable.

positions.isRequiredBasis: The NDA must contain all five of the following standard exclusions from the definition of "Confidential Information."
standardPosition: The NDA must contain all five of the following standard exclusions from the definition of "Confidential Information."
Information that is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a breach of the NDA by the Receiving Party or its Representatives.

The exclusion should be drafted to require that the information became publicly available through means other than a breach by the Receiving Party or any person to whom the Receiving Party disclosed the information.

Information that was already in the Receiving Party's possession prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as demonstrated by contemporaneous written records, and was not obtained directly or indirectly in violation of any confidentiality obligation owed to the Disclosing Party.

Information independently developed by the Receiving Party or its Representatives without reference to or use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, as demonstrated by contemporaneous written records.

Information received by the Receiving Party from a third party that is not, to the Receiving Party's knowledge, subject to a confidentiality obligation to the Disclosing Party with respect to such information.

Information that is required to be disclosed by applicable law, regulation, legal process, or governmental order, subject to compliance with the notice and cooperation provisions set forth in Section 6 of this playbook.

The exclusion should be conditioned on the Receiving Party providing prompt notice to the Disclosing Party (to the extent legally permissible) and reasonably cooperating with any effort by the Disclosing Party to obtain a protective order or other appropriate remedy.
walkAwayPosition: Verdantis will not execute an NDA that omits any of these exclusions without High Risk approval in accordance with Section 2.
The omission of any of the five standard exclusions listed above constitutes a walk-away position.

positions.isRequiredBasis: The term "Representatives" (or "Permitted Disclosees," depending on the counterparty's preferred nomenclature) must be defined broadly to include the Receiving Party's directors, officers, and employees, together with the following categories of external advisors and parties, in each case who have a need to know the Confidential Information in connection with evaluating or consummating the Transaction:
standardPosition: The term "Representatives" (or "Permitted Disclosees," depending on the counterparty's preferred nomenclature) must be defined broadly to include the Receiving Party's directors, officers, and employees, together with the following categories of external advisors and parties, in each case who have a need to know the Confidential Information in connection with evaluating or consummating the Transaction:
Legal counsel (including outside counsel retained by the Receiving Party for the Transaction or for related legal matters);
Financial advisors (including investment bankers, valuation consultants, and other financial advisors engaged by the Receiving Party);
Accounting advisors and auditors (including the Receiving Party's independent auditors and any accounting advisors specifically engaged for the Transaction);

Potential lenders and their respective advisors (including banks, financial institutions, and other credit providers that the Receiving Party may approach in connection with financing the Transaction, together with the legal, financial, and accounting advisors of such potential lenders);

Potential co-investors and their respective advisors (including equity co-investors, co-bidders, consortium members, and similar parties, together with their legal, financial, and accounting advisors).

The definition must be sufficiently broad to encompass Verdantis's existing advisor relationships and to ensure that Verdantis can share Confidential Information with the full range of professional advisors necessary to evaluate and, if applicable, consummate a Transaction.

text: If the counterparty insists on limiting the definition to an enumerated list of named categories rather than a general, open-ended formulation (e.g., "advisors and representatives who have a need to know"), Verdantis will accept a closed list provided that every category identified under the Preferred Position above is expressly included in the list.

In this scenario, Verdantis may also agree to a requirement that external advisors (i.e., advisors who are not directors, officers, or employees of the Receiving Party) be bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in the NDA, or that such advisors be bound by professional ethical obligations of confidentiality (as is the case for legal counsel and, in many jurisdictions, accounting professionals).

walkAwayPosition: Any definition of "Representatives" that would exclude either of these advisor categories — or their functional equivalents — is unacceptable.

A definition of "Representatives" or "Permitted Disclosees" that is limited to the Receiving Party's directors, officers, and employees only — and that excludes external legal counsel, financial advisors, potential lenders, and potential co-investors — constitutes a High Risk deviation and is unacceptable without approval from the General Counsel (Ramaswamy) and the VP, Corporate Development (Prescott).

positions.termName: Scope and Form of Confidential Information
positions.isRequiredBasis: The definition of "Confidential Information" should encompass information disclosed in any form, including written, oral, electronic, and visual.
standardPosition: The definition of "Confidential Information" should encompass information disclosed in any form, including written, oral, electronic, and visual.

The definition should be broad enough to capture technical data and specifications, financial information and projections, operational data and metrics, commercial terms and customer information, strategic plans and analyses, intellectual property and trade secrets, and personnel information, in each case to the extent disclosed by the Disclosing Party or its Representatives in connection with the Transaction.

The definition should also cover the fact that discussions or negotiations regarding the Transaction are occurring, the terms and conditions of those discussions, and the existence or content of any proposals or offers exchanged between the parties, in each case subject to the securities-law carve-out described in Section 6.1 of this playbook.

text: Verdantis may accept a reasonable narrowing of the scope of the definition to information that is marked or designated as "Confidential" (or words of similar import) at the time of disclosure, or within a specified time period following disclosure, provided that orally disclosed information is covered if the Disclosing Party provides written confirmation of the confidential nature of such information within 10 business days following the date of oral disclosure.

walkAwayPosition: A limitation of the definition of "Confidential Information" to written materials only — excluding oral, electronic, and visual disclosures — is unacceptable.

positions.isRequiredBasis: Verdantis's strong preference is for a mutual NDA under which both parties simultaneously function as Disclosing Party and Receiving Party.
standardPosition: Verdantis's strong preference is for a mutual NDA under which both parties simultaneously function as Disclosing Party and Receiving Party.

text: A unilateral NDA is acceptable where Verdantis is the Receiving Party only (i.e., where Verdantis is the potential acquiror and the counterparty is the potential target, and only the target is disclosing confidential information).
In this scenario, the scope of Verdantis's obligations as Receiving Party must be otherwise consistent with the positions set forth in this playbook.

walkAwayPosition: A unilateral NDA under which Verdantis is the Disclosing Party only, with no reciprocal confidentiality protection for information that the counterparty may disclose to Verdantis, is unacceptable.

positions.termName: Warranty Disclaimer and Accuracy of Information
positions.isRequiredBasis: Verdantis accepts and, in many cases, will affirmatively propose the inclusion of a provision disclaiming warranties as to the accuracy, completeness, or fitness for a particular purpose of the Confidential Information.
standardPosition: Verdantis accepts and, in many cases, will affirmatively propose the inclusion of a provision disclaiming warranties as to the accuracy, completeness, or fitness for a particular purpose of the Confidential Information.
However, any such disclaimer must include a savings clause expressly preserving claims for fraud or intentional misrepresentation.

text: If the counterparty resists the inclusion of an express fraud/intentional-misrepresentation savings clause — for example, on the ground that such a clause is unnecessary because fraud claims are not waivable as a matter of law — outside counsel should counter with alternative language providing that the warranty disclaimer does not apply to any representation or disclosure made by a party "with actual knowledge of its falsity."

walkAwayPosition: Outside counsel should not agree to any formulation — regardless of its placement in the NDA — that effectively immunizes a party against liability for fraud or intentional misrepresentation.

positions.termName: Term and Termination of the NDA
positions.isRequiredBasis: The NDA shall have a defined term of 12 months from the date of execution, during which period the parties may exchange Confidential Information in connection with evaluating and, if applicable, consummating the Transaction.
standardPosition: The NDA shall have a defined term of 12 months from the date of execution, during which period the parties may exchange Confidential Information in connection with evaluating and, if applicable, consummating the Transaction.
The NDA may also include a provision permitting either party to terminate the NDA at any time upon written notice to the other party.

In either case — whether the NDA expires at the end of its stated term or is terminated earlier — the confidentiality obligations set forth in the NDA shall survive termination or expiration in accordance with the survival period specified in Section 4.1.

text: Verdantis may accept a term of up to 18 months from the date of execution, particularly in complex transactions where the evaluation period is expected to be lengthy.
A term of between 12 and 18 months is a Low Risk deviation and may be approved by the Associate General Counsel (Castellano).

walkAwayPosition: An open-ended or "evergreen" term — i.e., a term that continues indefinitely with no expiration date and no termination mechanism — is unacceptable.

positions.isRequiredBasis: The return/destruction obligation must be subject to the following two carve-outs, both of which are required in every M&A NDA to which Verdantis is a party:
standardPosition: Upon the occurrence of a triggering event described in Section 5.1, the Receiving Party shall return to the Disclosing Party or destroy (at the Receiving Party's election) all Confidential Information, including all copies, notes, summaries, analyses, compilations, and other materials prepared by the Receiving Party or its Representatives that contain, reflect, or are derived from Confidential Information, within 15 business days of the triggering event.

Upon completion of such return or destruction, the Receiving Party shall provide a written certification of destruction signed by an authorized officer of the Receiving Party, in accordance with Section 5.3.
The return/destruction obligation must be subject to the following two carve-outs, both of which are required in every M&A NDA to which Verdantis is a party:

The Receiving Party may retain copies of Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or bona fide internal document-retention policy, or to the extent subject to a litigation hold, regulatory investigation, or other preservation obligation imposed by a court, regulatory authority, or the Receiving Party's legal counsel.
Such retained copies (collectively, "Retained Copies") remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of the NDA for the full duration of the applicable survival period set forth in Section 4.1.

The Receiving Party shall not be required to purge, delete, or otherwise remove Confidential Information from electronic archival, backup, or disaster-recovery systems (including, without limitation, disaster-recovery tapes, automated email archive systems, network backup servers, and similar systems) where deletion is not commercially practicable using reasonable efforts.

Confidential Information retained on such systems shall not be intentionally accessed by the Receiving Party or its Representatives following the return/destruction date and shall remain subject to the NDA's confidentiality obligations for the full duration of the applicable survival period.

text: Verdantis may accept a return/destruction timeline of no fewer than 10 business days following the triggering event, provided that both of the carve-outs described above (regulatory/legal holds and electronically archived copies) are retained in the NDA.

walkAwayPosition: A return/destruction deadline of fewer than 10 business days without the regulatory/legal-hold and electronic-archive carve-outs is classified as a Medium Risk deviation requiring approval from the General Counsel (Ramaswamy).

positions.termName: Non-Disclosure of Discussions / Existence of Transaction
positions.isRequiredBasis: The NDA shall include a provision restricting each party from disclosing to any third party the existence of the NDA, the fact that discussions or negotiations regarding the Transaction are occurring or have occurred, the terms or conditions of the Transaction under discussion, or the existence or content of any proposals, offers, or counteroffers exchanged between the parties (collectively, "Transaction Information").
standardPosition: The NDA shall include a provision restricting each party from disclosing to any third party the existence of the NDA, the fact that discussions or negotiations regarding the Transaction are occurring or have occurred, the terms or conditions of the Transaction under discussion, or the existence or content of any proposals, offers, or counteroffers exchanged between the parties (collectively, "Transaction Information").
However, the non-disclosure-of-discussions provision must contain a mandatory carve-out permitting disclosures of Transaction Information required under:

Applicable securities laws, including without limitation the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"), including Regulation FD;
Stock-exchange rules, including the rules and listing standards of the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC, given Verdantis's listing on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol VRDS;

Subpoena, court order, or other compulsory legal process, including civil or criminal subpoenas, regulatory demands, and orders or requests issued by any court, governmental authority, or self-regulatory organization.
In the event of any conflict between the NDA obligations and securities-law disclosure requirements, the securities-law obligations must control.

text: If the counterparty resists the inclusion of the full carve-out as described above, the minimum acceptable formulation must include, at a minimum, carve-outs for applicable securities laws and stock-exchange rules.

The non-solicitation restriction shall have a maximum duration of 12 months from the date of the NDA.
The non-solicitation restriction shall be limited to personnel of the Disclosing Party who are introduced to the Receiving Party in connection with the due diligence process for the Transaction.

The non-solicitation must not extend to personnel who are merely "contacted" during the due diligence process or whose names appear in documents, organizational charts, or other materials reviewed by the Receiving Party during diligence.
The non-solicitation provision must include the following standard carve-outs:

The non-solicitation shall not apply to solicitations resulting from general recruitment efforts, including job postings on the Receiving Party's website or third-party job boards, print or online advertisements of general circulation, and engagements of executive search firms, in each case that are not specifically directed at the Disclosing Party's personnel.

The non-solicitation shall not apply to personnel of the Disclosing Party who initiate contact with the Receiving Party or apply for employment with the Receiving Party without any solicitation by the Receiving Party.
Any non-solicitation provision must be subject to an actual-damages standard only.
Verdantis may accept a non-solicitation provision with a duration of up to 12 months and scope limited to personnel introduced in connection with the due diligence process.

In addition, Verdantis may accept a provision that restricts the Receiving Party from *hiring* (as opposed to merely *soliciting*) introduced personnel for up to 12 months, provided that the general-solicitation and unsolicited-contact exceptions described above are included.
In all cases, the actual-damages standard must be preserved and liquidated damages must not be accepted.

Verdantis will not agree to liquidated-damages provisions for non-solicitation breaches.

A non-solicitation (or no-hire) period exceeding 12 months in duration;
A non-solicitation scope that extends to any employee "contacted" during the due diligence process (as opposed to those "introduced" in connection with the process);
Any provision imposing liquidated damages for non-solicitation breaches, regardless of the amount of the stipulated damages.

text: If a standstill provision is commercially necessary to secure access to the counterparty's data room or to advance discussions to a stage where a transaction can be meaningfully evaluated, Verdantis may accept a standstill provision subject to all of the following conditions:
The standstill shall have a maximum duration of 12 months from the date of execution of the NDA.
The standstill shall automatically terminate, without notice or further action by either party, upon the earlier of:

The counterparty entering into a definitive agreement with any third party for a transaction involving the acquisition of a controlling interest in the counterparty (whether by merger, tender offer, asset acquisition, or otherwise); or

The counterparty commencing a public auction process, including without limitation by filing a proxy statement, issuing a press release, making a public announcement that it is exploring strategic alternatives or soliciting competing proposals, or otherwise publicly inviting third-party interest in acquiring the counterparty.

The standstill shall prohibit only the following actions: (i) acquiring, agreeing to acquire, or offering to acquire beneficial ownership of voting securities of the counterparty (other than through passive market purchases of less than a specified threshold); and (ii) making or publicly announcing any unsolicited proposal or offer for a merger, acquisition, business combination, or similar transaction involving the counterparty.

The standstill shall not restrict Verdantis from privately communicating with the counterparty's Board of Directors or senior management regarding a potential transaction, including making private proposals, requesting meetings, or expressing interest in a transaction, provided that such communications are not publicly disclosed by Verdantis.

walkAwayPosition: Verdantis will not accept a standstill period exceeding 12 months under any circumstances.

Acceptance of any standstill provision — even one conforming to all of the fallback parameters described above — constitutes a High Risk deviation and requires approval from both the General Counsel (Ramaswamy) and the VP, Corporate Development (Prescott).
In addition, the acceptance of any standstill provision triggers the board-level notification requirement described in Section 7.2 below.
The following are absolute walk-away positions that Verdantis will not accept under any circumstances, regardless of the commercial context:
A standstill period exceeding 12 months in duration;
A standstill without a mandatory fall-away provision of the type described above;
A standstill that restricts Verdantis from privately communicating with the counterparty's Board of Directors regarding a potential transaction;

"Don't ask, don't waive" provisions — i.e., provisions that prohibit Verdantis from requesting a waiver or modification of the standstill and/or prohibit the counterparty's Board of Directors from granting such a waiver, even if the Board determines that doing so would be in the best interests of the counterparty's shareholders.
